questions.calculus-section-10-5-49: Add the Moon radius to each altitude: nearest/farthest focus distances1838and2042km. Thena=(1838+2042)/2=1940,c=(2042−1838)/2=102,b²=a²−c². A translation/rotation gives equivalent equations; the stated convention fixes one.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-50: The focus liesp from the vertex and the latus-rectum opening is4p=10cm, sop=2.5. Atx=11, y=±√110, so diameter is2√110, not a radius.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-51: The earlier B signal meansPA−PB>0, selecting the right branch. Convert980ft/μs·1200μs to miles, then set this difference2a. Focaldistancec=200mi; atx=c, y=b²/a.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-52: Square the defining distance-difference relation twice, keeping both branches via the absolute value. The resulting positiveb² requiresc>a.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-53: Differentiate the positive square-root branch twice. Positivity ofa,b makes the numerator and denominator positive at everyx.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-54: The foci lie on the liney=x withc=√2. Majoraxislength4 givesa=2,b²=2. Rotate byπ/4 and expand.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-55: For the ellipse,c²=k−(k−16)=16. For the hyperbola,c²=k+(16−k)=16. Ifk<0 both squared-term denominators are negative, so their sum cannot equal1. k=0,16 are excluded undefined denominators.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-56: Implicit differentiation gives2yy′=4p. The tangent through(x₀,y₀), together withy₀²=4px₀, simplifies to the symmetric equation. At the vertex the tangent isx=0, consistent with the intercept.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-57: The tangent at(x₀,x₀²/(4p)) isx₀x=2py+x₀²/2. Substituting the directrix point produces the quadratic; its root product−4p² divided by(2p)² gives−1. Assume a nondegenerate parabolap≠0.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-58: The shared foci make the gradient of the sum of focal distances perpendicular to the gradient of their difference: (u₁+u₂)·(u₁−u₂)=|u₁|²−|u₂|²=0. Normals, hence tangents, are perpendicular at regular intersections.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-59: Exploit fourfold symmetry and apply the specified Simpson panel count to0≤t≤π/2. This convention is explicit because usingn panels on the entire0..2π interval gives a different finite-panel approximation. Arc speed is√(a²sin²t+b²cos²t).

questions.calculus-section-10-5-61: For the right focus, integrate2(b/a)√(x²−a²) fromx=a tox=c. The left focus gives the same area by symmetry. Use the standard radical primitive andc²−a²=b².
questions.calculus-section-10-5-62: Assumea≥b>0 are the major/minor semiaxes. Disk integration gives the ellipsoid volume4π times the product of its three semiaxes divided by3.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-63: The upper half ellipse has semiaxes2and3. Symmetry givesx̄=0; a half-ellipse centroid hasȳ=4b/(3π)=4/π, from the area and first moment integrals.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-64: Rotate the ellipse witha≥b>0. Use circumference times arc length; the prolate integral producesarcsin and the oblate integralatanh. At e=0 use the continuous limit instead of dividing byzero.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-65: The ellipse is a level set of the sum of distances to its foci. Its gradient is the sum of the corresponding unit vectors, which bisects their angle. Therefore their angles to the tangent are equal, giving reflection from one focus to the other.
questions.calculus-section-10-5-66: A hyperbola is a level set of the difference of focal distances. Its normal is the difference of unit focal vectors, while their sum is perpendicular to that normal. This angle-bisector geometry yields the stated equal tangent angles.
